ANSWER OF EXELON CORPORATION TO THE MOTION FOR EXPEDITED 
ACTION OF CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC 
(PUBLIC VERSION) 
Pursuant to Rule 2131 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission ("FERC" or "Commission"), Exelon Corporation on behalf of its 
subsidiaries2 (collectively, "Exelon") submits this Answer to the Motion for Expedited Action that 
was filed by Constellation Energy Generation, LLC ("Constellation") on November 21, 2025 
("Constellation's Motion").3
For the reasons discussed in the Answer of the Indicated PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
("PJM") Transmission Owners to Constellation's Motion, the Commission should reject 
Constellation's Motion.4 Exelon also files this Answer to correct any misapprehension regarding

I. 
REQUEST FOR CUU/PRIVIIIIC TREATMENT 
In accordance with section 388.112 of the Commission's regulations,5 Exelon requests 
privileged treatment for a portion of this Answer containing confidential information concerning 
pending retail customer service applications. Exelon understands that the involved customers may 
view this information as competitively sensitive and ComEd (the relevant Exelon utility) also treats 
such information as non-public. Accordingly, good cause exists for the Commission to grant this 
request for privileged treatment of this information. 
Exelon is filing both a public version of this Answer with necessary redactions and a non-
public version of this Answer that contains the confidential information. The non-public version 
has been labelled "CUI//PRIV//HC" and should be made subject to privileged document protection 
by the Commission. In accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 388.112(b)(2)(i), a proposed form of 
protective agreement modeled on the Commission's Model Protective Order is enclosed as 
Attachment A. To respect the competitive concerns of its customer, the Protective Order has been 
modified to provide additional protections for material deemed "Highly Confidential Privileged 
Material." Similar provisions have been included in other approved protective orders in recent 
years.' Any questions regarding this request for privileged treatment should be directed to the 
undersigned.

II. 
ANSWER 
In its motion, Constellation points to the Commission's statement that there are "allegations 
in the record that Exelon has delayed work on Constellation's requests to co-locate load with its 
generators at certain facilities due to Exelon's concerns that such requests are not allowed under 
the [PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff ("PJM Tariff')] without arranging for wholesale 
transmission or retail distribution service."' To be clear, these are merely allegations. Exelon has 
not "delayed" or refused service in response to any lawful request. 
In Attachment 1 of Exhibit 5 to Constellation's November 22, 2024 Complaint filed in 
Docket No. EL25-20-000,8 Constellation produced a November 12, 2024 letter from ComEd to 
Constellation concerning interconnection requests at the LaSalle and Byron nuclear facilities. In 
that letter, ComEd details certain design issues with Constellation's proposal and then explains 
that the "end use load is retail load under both Illinois and federal law and cannot be interconnected 
solely through amendments to the LaSalle or Byron [interconnection service agreements]."9
ComEd went on to explain: 
We continue to believe there is no lawful path to interconnect end 
use load at LaSalle and Byron without that load taking service as a 
retail customer of ComEd and we cannot continue to review 
proposals for co-location of end use load at LaSalle and Byron on 
some other basis.1°
at Attach. G (Sept. 22, 2025) (protective order in Federal Power Act section 205 filing with Highly Confidential 
Privileged Material provisions). 
See Constellation's Motion at 2 (citation omitted). 
8 
See Constellation, Complaint, Docket No. EL25-20. at Ex. 5 Attach. 1 (Nov. 22, 2024). 
9 
Id., Ex. 5 Attach. 1, at 2. 
10 
Id. 
3

PUBLIC VERSION 
ComEd appropriately suggested that Constellation move forward by making the requested design 
changes and submitting "an application for retail service."11 
The decision was left with 
Constellation. ComEd cannot unilaterally provide retail electric service to a customer that does 
not request it. 
Rather than deciding to move forward by then submitting an application for retail service 
(or attempting to challenge ComEd's assessment that this was retail service), Constellation instead 
decided to file its complaint seeking to change the PJM Tariff. Notwithstanding Constellation's 
allegations, the documentation submitted in this proceeding unambiguously shows that ComEd 
explained to Constellation how to move forward and how to do so expeditiously. It is Constellation 
that chose delay by disregarding Illinois retail regulation and established tariff mechanisms for 
entities that serve retail customers to obtain and ensure adequate transmission service. 
Constellation has chosen this path of litigation. 
The tariff changes that Constellation seeks in the pending motion are not necessary for 
large load interconnection requests to move forward, regardless of whether the load is proposed to 
be co-located with a generator or not. To the contrary, those requests are moving forward 
expeditiously, including in the Exelon footprint. Exelon agrees that "Nile United States' ability 
to remain at the forefront of technological innovation depends on a reliable supply of energy from 
all available electric generation sources and the integrity of our Nation's electric grid."12 Indeed, 
Exelon is furthering those efforts. As shown in the chart below, Exelon' s service territories have 
been and are projected to continue to be a focal point for data center interconnection.

new customers with relatively large forecasted demand,"" and at the time of his direct testimony, 
ComEd had 75 unique projects totaling over 28,000 megawatts ("MW") of maximum demand, 
i.e., approximately 4,000 MW higher than ComEd's all-time system peak demand in its 118-year 
hi story.14 Moreover, the Leichtman testimony notes that "the average size of a unique large

months prior to the testimony] [was] approximately 700 MWs, roughly equivalent to the demand 
of 1,400 big box retail stores."15
In ComEd's service territory, data center demand has grown at an annual rate of 27 percent 
through June 2025, and ComEd's most recent large load adjustment request to PJM included a 
future expected demand increase of 11 gigawatts ("GW") by 2040, 6 GW higher than ComEd's 
submission relative to the prior year.16 Moreover, the 2025 actuals year to date, as of September 
30, 2025, for historical on-peak hourly demand for data centers in the ComEd service territory in 
Northern Illinois was 600 MW.17 The foregoing underscores that Exelon is actively engaged in 
furthering the objectives of the Administration in the artificial intelligence race. 
In 2025, ComEd has received more than 25 customer service applications associated with 
requests for large load interconnections, representing new load in excess of 20 GW. These 
applications are moving forward, showing that Constellation is seeking a solution to a problem 
that does not exist. <BEGIN CUI//PRIV//HC> 
<END CUI//PRIV//HC> Any argument that co-located load applications are stalled or 
that the requested relief is somehow necessary to ensure that interconnections proceed is patently 
false.

PUBLIC VERSION 
Further, to leave no doubt that Exelon is working to help interconnect data centers, last 
month, in Docket No. ER25-3492-000, FERC issued an Order Accepting Transmission Security 
Agreement, an agreement by and between PECO and Amazon Data Services, Inc. ("Amazon"). 
Amazon is constructing a new data center campus in Falls Township, Pennsylvania, and PECO 
will provide retail electric delivery services for the data center campus, pursuant to its electric 
retail service tariff on file with the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission. In addition, Network 
Integrated Transmission Service will be procured by the responsible Load Serving Entity, as such 
term is defined in the PJM Tariff. The Transmission Security Agreement "ensures that a 
contribution to the transmission revenue requirement is made by Amazon commensurate with its 
requested end-use load relating to the construction of and service to its Data Center."18 This is 
another example of Exelon, in compliance with the PJM Tariff, providing a feasible path forward 
for data centers. 
Constellation's Motion and requested PJM Tariff changes are unwarranted and should be 
denied. 
18

PROTECTIVE AGREEMENT 
This Protective Agreement ("Agreement"), entered into this 
day of 
, 20_ by 
and between Exelon Corporation on behalf of its subsidiaries' ("Exelon") and  
("Intervenor"), shall govern the use of all Privileged, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, 
and/or Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information ("CEII") Material produced by Exelon 
to Intervenor, or vice versa, in connection with the captioned proceeding before the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission (the "Commission"). Exelon and Intervenor are sometimes referred to 
herein individually as a "Participant" or jointly as the "Participants." 
1. Exelon filed in the above-referenced proceeding Privileged Material, Highly Confidential 
Privileged Material, and/or CEII, as those terms are defined herein. 
Intervenor is a 
Participant in such proceeding, as the term Participant is defined in 18 C.F.R. Section 
385.102(b), or has filed a motion to intervene or a notice of intervention in such proceeding. 
Exelon and Intervenor enter into this Agreement to govern the use of Privileged Material, 
Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII produced by, or on behalf of, Exelon 
and/or Intervenor in the above-referenced proceeding. 
Notwithstanding any order 
terminating such proceeding, this Agreement shall remain in effect unless and until 
specifically modified or terminated by the Commission or a court of competent jurisdiction. 
In the event this Agreement terminates, the obligations of Reviewing Representatives to 
maintain the confidentiality of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, 
and/or CEII as provided hereunder shall remain in effect for 18 months following the date of 
termination. 
Exelon's subsidiaries are as follows: Atlantic City Electric Company, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company, 
Commonwealth Edison Company, Commonwealth Edison Company of Indiana, Inc., Delmarva Power and Light 
Company. PECO Energy Company, and Potomac Electric Power Company.

PUBLIC VERSION 
2. The Commission's regulations' and its policy governing the labelling of controlled 
unclassified information ("CUI")3 establish and distinguish the respective designations of 
Privileged Material and CEII. As to these designations, this Protective Agreement provides 
that a Participant: 
A. may designate as Privileged Material any material which customarily is treated 
by that Participant as commercially sensitive or proprietary or material subject 
to a legal privilege, which is not otherwise available to the public, and which if 
disclosed, would subject that Participant or its customers to risk of competitive 
disadvantage or other business injury; and 
B. must designate as CEII, any material that meets the definition of that term as 
provided by 18 C.F.R. §§ 388.113(a), (c). 
3. For the purposes of this Protective Agreement, the listed terms are defined as follows: 
A. Participant(s): As defined at 18 C.F.R. § 385.102(b). 
B. Privileged Material:4
i. 
Material (including depositions) provided by a Participant in response 
to discovery requests or filed with the Commission, and that is 
designated as Privileged Material by such Participant;5
ii. 
Material that is privileged under federal, state, or foreign law, such as 
work-product privilege, attorney-client privilege, or governmental 
privilege, and that is designated as Privileged Material by such 
Participant;6
Compare 18 C.F.R. § 388.112, with 18 C.F.R. § 388.113. This Protective Agreement does not alter the respective 
requirements imposed by these sections on Privileged Material or CEII. 
3 
Notice of Document Labelling Guidance for Documents Submitted to or Filed with the Commission or 
Commission Staff, 82 Fed. Reg. 18,632 (Apr. 20, 2017) (issued by Commission Apr. 14, 2017). 
4 
The Commission's regulations state that "[f]or the purposes of the Commission's filing requirements, non-CEII 
subject to an outstanding claim of exemption from disclosure under FOIA will be referred to as privileged 
material." 18 C.F.R. § 388.112(a). The regulations further state that "[f]or material filed in proceedings set for 
trial-type hearing or settlement judge proceedings, a participant's access to material for which privileged 
treatment is claimed is governed by the presiding official's protective order." Id. § 388.112(b)(2)(v). 
5 
See infra P 11 for the procedures governing the labeling of this designation. 
6 
The Commission's regulations state that "[a] presiding officer may, by order . . . restrict public disclosure of 
discoverable matter in order to . . . [p]reserve a privilege of a participant" 18 C.F.R. § 385.410(c)(3). To 
adjudicate such privileges, the regulations further state that "[i]n the absence of controlling Commission 
precedent, privileges will be determined in accordance with decisions of the Federal courts with due consideration 
to the Commission's need to obtain information necessary to discharge its regulatory responsibilities." Id. 
§ 385.410(d)(1)(i).

iii. 
Any information contained in or obtained from such designated 
material; 
iv. 
Any other material which is made subject to this Protective Agreement 
by the Presiding Administrative Law Judge (Presiding Judge) or the 
Chief Administrative Law Judge (Chief Judge) in the absence of the 
Presiding Judge or where no presiding judge is designated, the 
Commission, any court, or other body having appropriate authority, or 
by agreement of the Participants (subject to approval by the relevant 
authority); 
v. 
Notes of Privileged Material (memoranda, handwritten notes, or any 
other form of information (including electronic form) which copies or 
discloses Privileged Material);' or 
vi. 
Copies of Privileged Material. 
vii. 
Privileged Material does not include: 
1. Any information or document that has been filed with and accepted 
into the public files of the Commission, or contained in the public 
files of any other federal or state agency, or any federal or state 
court, unless the information or document has been determined to 
be privileged by such agency or court; or 
2. Information that is public knowledge, or which becomes public 
knowledge, other than through disclosure in violation of this 
Protective Agreement. 
C. Highly Confidential Privileged Material: A Participant may use this designation 
for those materials that are of such a commercially sensitive nature among the 
Participants or of such a private, personal nature that the producing Participant is 
able to justify a heightened level of confidential protection with respect to those 
materials. Highly Confidential Privileged Material shall include Privileged 
Material that present a higher risk of competitive injury if disclosed to 
Competitive Duty Personnel as determined in good faith by the producing 
Participant and includes materials such as: (1) information regarding contract 
negotiations and contract buyouts and (2) strategic business or financial plans. 
Except for the more limited list of persons who qualify as Reviewing 
Representatives for the purposes of Reviewing Highly Confidential Privileged 
Material (i.e., Reviewing Representatives that are not Competitive Duty 
Personnel), such materials are subject to the same provisions in the Protective 
Agreement as other Privileged Material. 
Notes of Privileged Material are subject to the same restrictions for Privileged Material except as specifically 
provided in this Protective Agreement. 
3

PUBLIC VERSION 
D. Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information ("CEII"): As defined at 18 
C.F.R. §§ 388.113(a), (c). 
E. Non-Disclosure Certificate: The certificate attached to this Protective 
Agreement, by which Participants granted access to Privileged Material, Highly 
Confidential Privileged Material, and or CEII must certify their understanding 
that such access to such material is provided pursuant to the terms and restrictions 
of this Protective Agreement, and that such Participants have read the Protective 
Agreement and agree to be bound by it. All executed Non-Disclosure Certificates 
must be served on all Participants on the official service list maintained by the 
Secretary of the Commission for this proceeding. 
F. Reviewing Representative: A person who has signed a Non-Disclosure 
Certificate and who is: 
i. 
Commission Trial Staff designated as such in this proceeding; 
ii. 
An attorney who has made an appearance in this proceeding for a 
Participant; 
iii. 
Attorneys, paralegals, and other employees associated for purposes of 
this case with an attorney who has made an appearance in this 
proceeding on behalf of a Participant; 
iv. 
An expert or an employee of an expert retained by a Participant for the 
purpose of advising, preparing for, submitting evidence or testifying in 
this proceeding; 
v. 
A person designated as a Reviewing Representative by order of the 
Presiding Judge, the Chief Judge, or the Commission; or 
vi. 
Employees or other representatives of Participants appearing in this 
proceeding with significant responsibility for this docket. 
G. The term "Reviewing Representative" for purposes of reviewing Highly 
Confidential Privileged Material defined in Paragraph 3(C) shall mean a person 
who has signed a Non-Disclosure Certificate who is: 
i. 
Listed in Paragraph 3(F), but is not Competitive Duty Personnel as 
defined in Paragraph 3(H); or 
ii. 
Designated as a Reviewing Representative for purposes of reviewing 
Highly Confidential Privileged Material by agreement of the producing 
Participant or by order of the Presiding Judge. 
H. The term "Competitive Duty Personnel" shall mean any individual(s) whose 
scope of employment or engagement includes the marketing, sale, or purchase 
of coal, natural gas, or electricity (collectively, "Energy"), the direct

PUBLIC VERSION 
supervision of any employee or employees whose duties include the marketing 
of Energy, or other Energy services in competition with the producing 
Participant, all of which are considered "Competitive Duties," except that 
Competitive Duty Personnel shall not include employees of the Commission, 
any state utilities commission which is a Participant, in-house or outside 
counsel, and/or an outside consultant retained by a Participant for the purpose 
of advising, preparing for, submitting evidence, or testifying in this proceeding. 
4. Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII shall be made 
available under the terms of this Protective Agreement only to Participants and only to their 
Reviewing Representatives as provided in Paragraphs 6-10 of this Protective Agreement. 
The contents of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, CEII or any 
other form of information that copies or discloses such materials shall not be disclosed to 
anyone other than in accordance with this Protective Agreement and shall be used only in 
connection with this specific proceeding. 
5. All Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and or CEII must be 
maintained in a secure place. Access to those materials must be limited to Reviewing 
Representatives specifically authorized pursuant to Paragraphs 7-9 of this Protective 
Agreement. 
6. Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII must be handled 
by each Participant and by each Reviewing Representative in accordance with the Non-
Disclosure Certificate executed pursuant to Paragraph 9 of this Protective Agreement. 
Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII shall not be used 
except as necessary for the conduct of this proceeding, nor shall they (or the substance of 
their contents) be disclosed in any manner to any person except a Reviewing 
Representative who is engaged in this proceeding and who needs to know the information 
in order to carry out that person's responsibilities in this proceeding. A Reviewing 
Representative shall not disclose Highly Confidential Privileged Material to Competitive 
Duty Personnel, except as authorized pursuant to Paragraph 3(G). 
Reviewing 
Representatives may make copies of Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged 
Material, and/or CEII, but such copies automatically become Privileged Material, Highly 
Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII. Reviewing Representatives may make 
notes of Privileged Material, which shall be treated as Notes of Privileged Material if they 
reflect the contents of Privileged Material. 
7. If a Reviewing Representative's scope of employment includes any of the activities listed 
under this Paragraph 7, such Reviewing Representative may not use information contained 
in any Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII obtained 
in this proceeding for a commercial purpose (e.g., to give a Participant or competitor of 
any Participant a commercial advantage): 
A. Energy marketing; 
B. Direct supervision of any employee or employees whose duties include energy 
marketing; or 
5

PUBLIC VERSION 
C. The provision of consulting services to any person whose duties include energy 
marketing. 
8. If a Participant wishes to designate a person not described in Paragraph 3(F) above as a 
Reviewing Representative, the Participant must seek agreement from the Participant 
providing the Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII. 
If an agreement is reached, the designee shall be a Reviewing Representative pursuant to 
Paragraph 3(E) of this Protective Agreement with respect to those materials. If no 
agreement is reached, the matter must be submitted to the Presiding Judge or the 
Commission for resolution. 
9. A Reviewing Representative shall not be permitted to inspect, participate in discussions 
regarding, or otherwise be permitted access to Privileged Material, Highly Confidential 
Privileged Material, and/or CEII pursuant to this Protective Agreement until three business 
days after that Reviewing Representative first has executed and served a Non-Disclosure 
Certificate.8 However, if an attorney qualified as a Reviewing Representative has executed 
a Non-Disclosure Certificate, any participating paralegal, secretarial and clerical personnel 
under the attorney's instruction, supervision or control need not do so. 
Attorneys 
designated Reviewing Representatives are responsible for ensuring that persons under their 
supervision or control comply with this Protective Agreement, and must take all reasonable 
precautions to ensure that Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, 
and/or CEII are not disclosed to unauthorized persons. Reviewing Representatives that are 
Competitive Duty Personnel as defined in Paragraph 3(H) must execute a Non-Disclosure 
Certificate for Competitive Duty Personnel in the form attached hereto. All executed Non-
Disclosure Certificates must be served on all Participants on the official service list 
maintained by the Secretary of the Commission for the proceeding. 
10. Any Reviewing Representative may, consistent with the requirements in Paragraph 3(G), 
disclose Privileged Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII to any 
other Reviewing Representative as long as both Reviewing Representatives have executed a 
Non-Disclosure Certificate. In the event any Reviewing Representative to whom Privileged 
Material, Highly Confidential Privileged Material, and/or CEII are disclosed ceases to 
participate in this proceeding, or becomes employed or retained for a position that renders him 
or her ineligible to be a Reviewing Representative under Paragraph 3(F) of this Protective 
Agreement, access to such materials by that person shall be terminated. Even if no longer 
engaged in this proceeding, every person who has executed a Non-Disclosure Certificate shall 
continue to be bound by the provisions of this Protective Agreement and the Non-Disclosure 
Certificate for as long as the Protective Agreement is in effect.'

13. Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall be construed as precluding any Participant from
